meta.source_regulations: IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 (as amended up to 12 Jan 2026)
meta.scope: All eleven CMI categories: Part A (universal) + category-specific Part B for every registration type
meta.disclaimer: This is a self-assessment aid, not an audit or an IFSCA determination. The independent Compliance Auditor's examination under Regulation 25 of the IFSCA (Capital Market Intermediaries) Regulations, 2025 remains the only legally operative compliance opinion.
meta.engine_note: Applicability is regulation-driven: mandatory controls offer Yes/No only; 'Not applicable' is available solely where the regulation makes the obligation event-based or activity-conditional. Every outcome states the regulatory requirement with clause reference and justification.

engine.principle: Regulation-driven, not answer-echoing. The participant's Yes/No is only an INPUT; the verdict and its justification are anchored to the requirement and cite the clause. 'Not applicable' is reachable ONLY for controls whose nature is 'event' or 'activity_conditional'. Mandatory controls offer Yes/No only and can never be marked N/A by the participant.
engine.readiness_formula: readiness_pct = round(green / (green + amber + red) * 100); 0 when denominator is 0
engine.risk_weighted_open: sum of risk_weights[risk_weight] over every control whose computed code is 'amber' or 'red'
compute_algorithm: INPUT: control, answer{primary, ev[], suff{index:'y'|'n'}, rotFY}, fy_under_review
2. if primary == 'no': return 'red' when nature=='mandatory', else 'na' (obligation not triggered)
3a. PA-28 rotation override: years = int(fy[:4]) - int(rotFY[:4]) + 1; if years>3 -> 'red'; if years==3 -> set amber_floor=true
3b. for each index in control.critical_suff: if suff[index]=='n' -> 'red'
3d. hasEvidence = any selected evidence index >= 0; if not hasEvidence -> 'amber'
3e. if number of answered sufficiency questions < total sufficiency questions -> 'amber' (incomplete)

outcome_templates.caveat: The Compliance Auditor's independent examination under Regulation 25 remains the only legally operative opinion.
outcome_templates.green: {basis} Your responses indicate this is in place and evidenced. Basis: {ref}. {caveat}
outcome_templates.amber: {basis} You have indicated it is addressed, but the supporting evidence or checks are still incomplete - close this before your audit. Basis: {ref}.
outcome_templates.red: {basis} Your response indicates the requirement may not be met. Prioritise remediation and flag it to your Compliance Auditor. Basis: {ref}.
outcome_templates.na: This obligation is triggered only where {condition}. You have indicated it did not arise, so it is not triggered. Basis: {ref}.

control_schema.clause_ref: string, statutory citation shown to user and in outputs
control_schema.condition: string|null, the regulatory trigger for event/activity_conditional (used in N/A outcome)
control_schema.regulatory_basis: one-line statement of what the clause requires (anchors every outcome)
control_schema.evidence_options: string[] shown as 'what could you show an auditor?'
control_schema.critical_suff: int[] indices of sufficiency_questions where a 'No' escalates to 'red'

controls.requirement_text: Maintain the Schedule I minimum net worth for your category at all times. Amounts: Credit Rating Agency USD 200,000; Custodian USD 1 million; Debenture Trustee USD 1.5 million; Distributor USD 50,000; ESG Ratings & Data Products Provider, Investment Adviser and Research Entity USD 25,000 each; Investment Banker USD 100,000; Broker Dealer, Clearing Member and Depository Participant as specified by the recognised stock exchange / clearing corporation / depository. For a broker dealer, clearing member or investment banker, net worth means liquid assets (cash, bank, FDs, G-Secs); for all other categories it is accounting net worth. A branch may hold the minimum at parent level, earmarked for the IFSC branch. An entity in multiple categories maintains the highest applicable minimum.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 7 read with Schedule I requires the minimum net worth for the category(ies) held to be maintained at all times; for a broker dealer, clearing member or investment banker it is computed on a liquid-assets basis under Reg 3(1)(cc).
controls.question_primary: Did your net worth stay at or above the prescribed minimum throughout the FY under review?
controls.question_why: Net worth is a registration-level floor the Authority monitors closely. Slipping below it, even for part of the year, is a reportable breach.
evidence_options: Bank / FD / G-Sec statements backing liquid assets
sufficiency_questions: Is it computed on the liquid-assets basis applicable to you?
Did it stay above the minimum at every quarter-end, not just year-end?

controls.requirement_text: Remain present in the IFSC in a permitted legal form: a company, an LLP, a body corporate, or a branch thereof.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 6 permits a CMI to operate only as a company, LLP, body corporate, or a branch thereof, in the IFSC.
controls.question_primary: Is your entity present in the IFSC in a permitted legal form (company, LLP, body corporate, or branch)?
controls.question_why: Only these legal forms may hold a CMI registration; a change in form the Authority is unaware of unsettles your registration.
sufficiency_questions: Has the legal form remained unchanged during the FY?

controls.requirement_text: Ensure the entity and its principal officer, directors/partners, KMP and controlling shareholders are fit and proper at all times, free of the listed disqualifications.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 8 requires the entity and its PO, directors/partners, KMP and controlling shareholders to be fit and proper at all times.
controls.question_primary: Are the entity and all covered persons fit and proper, with no disqualifying event during the FY under review?
controls.question_why: Fit-and-proper status must hold at all times; a disqualifying event against any covered person can jeopardise the registration itself.
sufficiency_questions: Do you hold current declarations from every covered person?
Can you confirm no disqualifying event (conviction, charge-sheet, regulatory order, wilful-defaulter tag) arose during the FY?

controls.requirement_text: Designate a Principal Officer, based out of the IFSC, meeting the qualification route and at least 3 years' financial-services experience; the PO carries overall responsibility for CMI operations.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 9 requires a Principal Officer, based out of the IFSC, meeting the prescribed qualification and at least 3 years' financial-services experience.
controls.question_primary: Have you designated an IFSC-based Principal Officer who meets the qualification and 3-year experience requirements?
controls.question_why: The PO carries overall responsibility for your CMI operations; an eligibility shortfall weakens every filing the PO signs.
sufficiency_questions: Does the PO meet the qualification route (professional membership / PG degree / graduate + 5 yrs)?
Does the PO have at least 3 years' financial-services experience?
Is the PO based out of the IFSC?

If you hold multiple registrations, is a separate PO designated where required (one PO may be shared only across broker dealer, clearing member, depository participant, investment adviser, research entity, custodian and distributor; and across CRA and ERDPP)?

controls.requirement_text: Designate a separate Compliance Officer, based out of the IFSC, meeting the qualification route (incl. LLB) and at least 2 years' experience (financial-services or compliance).
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 9 requires a separate Compliance Officer, based out of the IFSC, meeting the prescribed qualification and at least 2 years' experience.
controls.question_primary: Have you designated a separate, IFSC-based Compliance Officer who meets the qualification and 2-year experience requirements?
controls.question_why: The CO must be a distinct, empowered person; combining or under-qualifying the role is a common inspection finding.
sufficiency_questions: Is the CO a different person from the PO?
Does the CO meet the qualification route?
Does the CO have at least 2 years' experience (financial-services or compliance)?

controls.requirement_text: Maintain manpower adequate for, and commensurate with, the scale and nature of the CMI's IFSC activities.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 9(6) requires manpower adequate for, and commensurate with, the CMI's IFSC activities.
controls.question_primary: Do you have manpower adequate for the scale and nature of your IFSC activities?
controls.question_why: Thin staffing is treated as an operational-risk gap; the Authority expects headcount and skills to match what you actually do.
sufficiency_questions: Are the compliance, operations and business functions each staffed?
Is headcount proportionate to your activity volume and mix?

controls.requirement_text: Ensure employees complete the certification courses specified by the Authority, where any are specified for the activity.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 9(5) requires employees to complete the certification courses specified by the Authority.
controls.question_primary: Have your employees completed the certification courses specified by the Authority (where any apply to your activity)?
controls.question_why: Where the Authority mandates certifications, uncertified staff in covered roles is a straightforward finding.
evidence_options: Confirmation that no certification is currently specified for your category
sufficiency_questions: Have you checked whether any certification is currently specified for your category?
Do covered employees hold the required certification?

controls.requirement_text: Maintain and preserve the full set of books, records and documents in retrievable electronic form for at least 8 years, including the quarterly net-worth statement, AML/KYC documentation, client account docs, and complaint records.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 16 requires books, records and documents to be maintained in electronic retrievable form for at least 8 years.
controls.question_primary: Are you maintaining the full set of books, records and documents in retrievable electronic form for at least 8 years?
controls.question_why: Retention is its own obligation; missing or unretrievable records are a finding regardless of whether the underlying activity was compliant.
evidence_options: Sample records (balance sheet, P&L, auditor report, quarterly net-worth statement)
sufficiency_questions: Is retention set to at least 8 years (or from inception if newer)?
Are records held in electronic, retrievable form?
Does the set cover all sub-items, including the quarterly net-worth statement and AML documentation?

controls.requirement_text: Maintain a Business Continuity Plan commensurate with size/nature/scale, update it on material change, and review it annually.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 20 requires a Business Continuity Plan, updated on material change and reviewed annually.
controls.question_primary: Do you have a Business Continuity Plan that you review annually and update on material change?
controls.question_why: A BCP that exists on paper but was never reviewed or tested rarely satisfies an auditor.
sufficiency_questions: Is the BCP approved by the board / management?
Has it been reviewed within the last 12 months?
Is it updated when operations, structure, business or location change?

controls.requirement_text: Maintain a robust cyber security and cyber resilience framework meeting the Authority's requirements (currently the IFSCA CSCRF circular), including the time-bound self-certification.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 21 requires a cyber security and resilience framework meeting the Authority's requirements, currently the CSCRF.
controls.question_primary: Do you have a cyber security and resilience framework aligned to the IFSCA CSCRF requirements?
controls.question_why: Cyber resilience is an active supervisory theme; the CSCRF sets specific expectations and its self-certification is time-bound.
sufficiency_questions: Is the framework mapped to the applicable CSCRF requirements?
Have you filed the CSCRF self-certification where required?
Is there evidence of testing (e.g., VAPT)?

controls.requirement_text: Maintain a sound, documented risk management system that is in use.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 22(1) requires a sound risk management system.
controls.question_primary: Do you have a documented risk management system that is actually in use?
controls.question_why: The Authority expects risks to be identified and managed through a defined system, not handled informally.
sufficiency_questions: Is the system documented and approved?
Is there a live risk register or equivalent?

controls.requirement_text: Maintain adequate internal controls and procedures, including over any outsourced activities, to protect client interests and manage risk.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 22(2) requires adequate internal controls and procedures, including over outsourced activities.
controls.question_primary: Do you have adequate internal controls and procedures, including over any outsourced activities?
controls.question_why: Internal controls are what protect client interests and assets day to day; gaps here surface quickly on inspection.
sufficiency_questions: Do the controls cover your outsourced activities?
Are they reviewed or tested periodically?

controls.requirement_text: Maintain and operate an AML/CFT/KYC framework compliant with the IFSCA (AML, CTF and KYC) Guidelines, 2022, with the designated officer and screening/STR records.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 16(1)(e) requires compliance with the IFSCA (AML, CTF and KYC) Guidelines, 2022 and retention of related documentation.
controls.question_primary: Do you have an AML/CFT/KYC framework compliant with the IFSCA AML, CTF & KYC Guidelines, 2022?
controls.question_why: AML is among the highest-consequence areas; expect close scrutiny of the policy, the designated officer and screening records.
sufficiency_questions: Is the policy aligned to the 2022 IFSCA AML Guidelines?
Have you designated the required AML officer(s)?
Do you retain screening and, where applicable, STR records?

controls.requirement_text: Maintain a working investor grievance redressal mechanism as specified by the Authority.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 18 requires adequate steps for investor grievance redressal as specified by the Authority.
controls.question_primary: Do you have a working investor grievance redressal mechanism?
controls.question_why: A mechanism that exists but shows no activity log is hard to evidence; auditors look for the process and its operation.
sufficiency_questions: Is the mechanism documented?
Is there a register capturing complaints and their resolution?

controls.requirement_text: Adopt the dispute-resolution mechanism specified by the Authority for client/investor disputes.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 19 requires client/investor disputes to be handled under the Authority's specified dispute-resolution mechanism.
controls.question_primary: Have you adopted the dispute-resolution mechanism specified by the Authority for client/investor disputes?
controls.question_why: Client disputes must route through the specified mechanism, not ad-hoc handling.
sufficiency_questions: Do your client terms reference the specified mechanism?
Is there a defined process for disputes that arise?

controls.requirement_text: Maintain an internal outsourcing policy for activities outsourced from outside the IFSC and comply with it at all times.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part A (cl. 18) requires an internal outsourcing policy for activities outsourced from outside the IFSC, with ongoing compliance.
controls.question_primary: Do you have an internal outsourcing policy for activities outsourced from outside the IFSC, and do you comply with it?
controls.question_why: Outsourcing without a governing policy is a specific Code-of-Conduct gap.
sufficiency_questions: Does the policy cover all activities you outsource from outside the IFSC?
Do your outsourcing arrangements comply with it?

controls.requirement_text: Adopt an internal code of conduct governing internal operations and employee conduct.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part A (cl. 19) requires an internal code of conduct governing operations and employees.
controls.question_primary: Have you adopted an internal code of conduct governing your operations and employees?
controls.question_why: This is a required internal document, distinct from the regulatory Code of Conduct in Schedule II.
sufficiency_questions: Is the internal code documented and approved?
Have employees acknowledged it?

controls.requirement_text: Operationalise adherence to the Schedule II Part A Code of Conduct (integrity, fair dealing, no market abuse, no insider trading, suitability, senior-management responsibility).
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 15 requires adherence to the Code of Conduct in Schedule II Part A.
controls.question_primary: Do you have processes ensuring adherence to the Schedule II Part A Code of Conduct across the firm?
controls.question_why: The Code is tested on whether it is operationalised, not merely adopted.
evidence_options: Supporting policies (insider trading, suitability, fair dealing)
sufficiency_questions: Is adherence supported by specific policies and processes?
Is there evidence of training or monitoring?

controls.requirement_text: Identify, disclose and resolve conflicts of interest through a defined mechanism with a record.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part A (cl. 9) requires conflicts of interest to be avoided, disclosed and resolved through a mechanism.
controls.question_primary: Do you identify, disclose and resolve conflicts of interest through a defined process?
controls.question_why: Conflicts must be managed through a mechanism with a record; informal handling does not evidence well.
sufficiency_questions: Is there a documented COI process?
Is there a register capturing disclosures and how conflicts were handled?

controls.requirement_text: Maintain measures ensuring client information stays confidential except where the law requires disclosure.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part A (cl. 8) requires client information to be kept confidential except where disclosure is required by law.
controls.question_primary: Do you have measures ensuring client information stays confidential except where the law requires disclosure?
controls.question_why: Client confidentiality is a Code obligation; access controls and staff undertakings are the usual evidence.
sufficiency_questions: Is confidentiality covered by policy?
Are there controls limiting who can access client information?

controls.requirement_text: Ensure the Compliance Officer has adequate freedom and power to discharge the role, with a reporting line to the board/governing body.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part A (cl. 20) requires the Compliance Officer to be given adequate freedom and power.
controls.question_primary: Has the board given the Compliance Officer adequate freedom and power to discharge the role?
controls.question_why: A CO without authority or board reporting access is a governance red flag the Authority looks for.
evidence_options: CO reporting line to board / governing body
sufficiency_questions: Does the CO report to the board or governing body?
Is the CO's authority documented?

controls.condition: a material change to previously-furnished registration information arises
controls.requirement_text: Furnish to the Authority any material change in previously-furnished information bearing on the certificate of registration.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 17(1) requires any material change in previously-furnished information bearing on registration to be furnished to the Authority.
controls.question_primary: Did any material change to previously-furnished registration information arise this FY?
controls.question_why: Material changes bearing on your registration must reach the Authority; silence is the breach.
evidence_options: Intimation letter / email to the Authority
sufficiency_questions: Did the intimation cover all details bearing on the registration?
Was the intimation made promptly after the change?

controls.condition: a change in Principal Officer, Compliance Officer or KMP occurs
controls.requirement_text: Intimate the Authority of any change in Principal Officer, Compliance Officer or KMP within 15 days.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 17(2) requires any change in PO, CO or KMP to be intimated to the Authority within 15 days.
controls.question_primary: Did your Principal Officer, Compliance Officer or KMP change this FY?
controls.question_why: Key-person changes carry a hard 15-day clock; a correct change filed late still counts against you.
sufficiency_questions: Did it cover every changed key person?
Was the intimation made within 15 days of the change?

controls.condition: a direct or indirect change in control occurs
controls.requirement_text: On change in control, follow the correct route: an IFSC-incorporated CMI seeks PRIOR approval; a branch intimates within 15 days.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 23 requires prior approval for a change in control of an IFSC-incorporated CMI, and 15-day intimation for a branch.
controls.question_primary: Did a direct or indirect change in control occur this FY?
controls.question_why: An IFSC-incorporated CMI needs prior approval; a branch must intimate within 15 days. Getting the route or timing wrong is a serious lapse.
evidence_options: Board / shareholder records evidencing the change
sufficiency_questions: Was the correct route used for your legal form?
Was prior approval obtained before the change (incorporated) / intimation made within 15 days (branch)?

controls.requirement_text: Furnish all reports, returns and statements in the manner, interval and form specified by the Authority, including periodic/quarterly reporting, by their due dates.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 17(3) requires reports, returns and statements to be furnished in the manner, interval and form specified by the Authority.
controls.question_primary: Have you filed all reports, returns and statements specified by the Authority for the FY, on time (including any quarterly reporting)?
controls.question_why: Fixed-calendar filings are the easiest thing for the Authority to check, and late or missed returns are a common warning-letter trigger.
sufficiency_questions: Are all periods covered with no gaps?
Were all required filings made on or before their due dates?

controls.requirement_text: Pay annual fees, turnover-based fees and any other fees specified by the Authority by their due dates.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 24 requires payment of annual fees, turnover-based fees and other specified fees.
controls.question_primary: Have you paid your annual fees, turnover-based fees and any other specified fees for the FY?
controls.question_why: Fee defaults are simple to detect and reflect poorly on basic compliance discipline.
sufficiency_questions: Were all applicable fee heads paid?
Were they paid by the due dates?

controls.requirement_text: File the ACAR together with the ACAC by 30 September for the preceding FY, with the Authority, and with the MII if you are a broker dealer / clearing member / depository participant.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 25 read with the ACAR Circular requires the ACAR with the ACAC to be filed by 30 September for the preceding FY (and with the MII for a BD/CM/DP).
controls.question_primary: Are you on track to file the ACAR together with the ACAC by 30 September for the FY under review?
controls.question_why: This is the filing the whole exercise leads to; missing 30 September or omitting the MII copy is a direct lapse.
sufficiency_questions: Is the audit on track to be completed and filed by 30 September?
If you are a BD/CM/DP, will a copy also go to your MII?

controls.requirement_text: Appoint an eligible Compliance Auditor: peer-reviewed ICAI/ICSI/ICMAI (or foreign-authorised), independent with no conflict, appointed for at most 3 consecutive years with a 2-year cooling-off before reappointment.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 25(1) and the ACAR Circular require a peer-reviewed, independent Compliance Auditor, appointed for at most 3 consecutive years with a 2-year cooling-off.
controls.question_primary: Is your Compliance Auditor eligible: peer-reviewed (or foreign-authorised), independent, and within the 3 consecutive-year cap?
controls.question_why: The auditor's eligibility underpins the entire report; peer-review status, independence and rotation limits are all checkable.
sufficiency_questions: Is the auditor a peer-reviewed member (or foreign-authorised)?
Is the auditor independent with no conflict of interest?

controls.requirement_text: Be positioned to cooperate fully with an inspection: records retrievable, premises accessible, and staff available to assist.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 38 requires the CMI to cooperate fully with an inspection.
controls.question_primary: Are you positioned to cooperate fully with an inspection (records retrievable, premises accessible, staff available)?
controls.question_why: Non-cooperation is itself a ground for action, separate from any underlying issue.
evidence_options: Named point of contact for inspections
sufficiency_questions: Can you produce books, records and documents on request?
Is there a named person to coordinate an inspection?

controls.condition: penal action, a registration-status change, or a material adverse financial change arises
controls.requirement_text: On penal action, registration-status change, or material adverse financial change, promptly inform the Authority and affected clients.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part A (cl. 12-13) requires prompt intimation of penal action, registration-status change or material adverse financial change to the Authority and affected clients.
controls.question_primary: Did any penal action, registration-status change, or material adverse financial change arise this FY?
controls.question_why: These events must reach the Authority and clients promptly; delayed disclosure compounds the original issue.
sufficiency_questions: Were affected clients informed where required?
Was the Authority informed promptly?

controls.requirement_text: For each managed issue, sign an agreement with the issuer setting out the IB's roles and responsibilities.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 35(1) requires an agreement with the issuer specifying the IB's roles and responsibilities in the issue.
controls.question_primary: For each issue you manage, do you sign an agreement with the issuer setting out your roles and responsibilities?
controls.question_why: The engagement agreement is the baseline document for an IB mandate; its absence is an obvious gap.
sufficiency_questions: Is an agreement in place for every managed issue?
Does it clearly set out roles and responsibilities?

controls.condition: more than one lead investment banker acts on an issue
controls.requirement_text: Where more than one lead investment banker acts on an issue, clearly demarcate each lead's responsibilities.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 35(2) requires responsibilities of each lead IB to be clearly demarcated where more than one lead acts.
controls.question_primary: Do multiple lead investment bankers ever act together on your issues?
controls.question_why: Overlapping or undefined lead responsibilities create accountability gaps the Authority dislikes.
sufficiency_questions: Is there a written allocation of responsibilities where multiple leads act?

controls.condition: you are a promoter or associate of the issuer
controls.requirement_text: Where the IB is a promoter or associate of the issuer, restrict its role to marketing of the issue only.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 35(3) restricts an IB that is a promoter or associate of the issuer to marketing of the issue only.
controls.question_primary: Are you ever a promoter or associate of an issuer whose issue you manage?
controls.question_why: Acting beyond marketing when you are connected to the issuer is a hard conflict-of-interest breach.
evidence_options: Evidence that scope was limited to marketing where connected
sufficiency_questions: Do you screen whether you are a promoter/associate of the issuer?
Where connected, was your role limited to marketing?

controls.requirement_text: Maintain controls preventing the IB and its officers, directors, partners, managers, associates and relatives from dealing in an issuer's securities on the basis of UPSI.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 35(4) prohibits the IB and its officers, partners, associates and relatives from dealing in the issuer's securities on UPSI.
controls.question_primary: Do you have controls preventing dealing in an issuer's securities on the basis of UPSI by you and your connected persons?
controls.question_why: UPSI misuse is among the gravest capital-markets offences; the Authority expects hard controls, not just a policy line.
sufficiency_questions: Does the policy cover the IB, its officers, directors, partners, associates and relatives?
Are there operational controls (restricted list / trading window / pre-clearance)?

controls.condition: you acquire securities of an issuer whose issue you are managing
controls.requirement_text: Where the IB acquires securities of a managed issuer, file complete particulars with the Authority within 15 days.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 35(5) requires particulars of any acquisition of a managed issuer's securities to be filed with the Authority within 15 days.
controls.question_primary: Did you acquire securities of any issuer whose issue you were managing this FY?
controls.question_why: This is a specific 15-day disclosure; narrow, but missing it is a clear reporting breach.
evidence_options: Filing of transaction particulars to the Authority
sufficiency_questions: Did the filing include complete particulars?
Was the filing made within 15 days of the transaction?

controls.requirement_text: Keep total underwriting obligations across all agreements within 20 times the IB's net worth at all times.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 35(6)(b) caps total underwriting obligations at 20 times the IB's net worth at all times.
controls.question_primary: Do you undertake underwriting?
controls.question_why: The 20x cap is a hard quantitative limit; breaching it exposes the firm well beyond its capacity.
sufficiency_questions: Do you track aggregate underwriting obligations against 20x net worth?
Has the aggregate stayed within the cap at all times?

controls.requirement_text: Where underwriting, sign an agreement with the issuer covering underwriting amount, commission, duties and timelines.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 35(6)(a) requires an underwriting agreement covering amount, commission, duties and timelines.
controls.question_primary: Do you undertake underwriting?
controls.question_why: An underwriting commitment without a proper agreement is both a compliance and a commercial risk.
evidence_options: Terms covering amount, commission, duties and timelines
sufficiency_questions: Is an agreement in place for each underwriting?
Does it cover amount, commission, duties and timelines?

controls.requirement_text: Ensure investors get adequate, timely disclosures to make a balanced, informed decision.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(H)(1) requires adequate, timely disclosures to investors for a balanced, informed decision.
controls.question_primary: Do you ensure investors get adequate, timely disclosures to make a balanced, informed decision?
controls.question_why: Adequate disclosure is the core investor-protection duty for an IB; thin or late disclosure is a finding.
evidence_options: Records of disclosures made to investors
sufficiency_questions: Are disclosures made in line with applicable regulations/guidelines?
Are they timely?

controls.requirement_text: Provide investors true and adequate information, free of misleading or exaggerated claims, and ensure awareness of risk.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(H)(2) requires true and adequate information without misleading or exaggerated claims, and investor awareness of risk.
controls.question_primary: Do you ensure investors receive true and adequate information, free of misleading or exaggerated claims, and are made aware of risks?
controls.question_why: Misleading or exaggerated claims are a direct conduct breach and a reputational and enforcement risk.
evidence_options: Content review / sign-off process for investor materials
sufficiency_questions: Is there a review process for accuracy of investor materials?
Are risk factors clearly conveyed?

controls.requirement_text: Ensure the prospectus / offer document / letter of offer is available to investors at the time of the issue or offer.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(H)(3) requires the prospectus/offer document/letter of offer to be available to investors at the issue/offer.
controls.question_primary: Do you ensure the offer document is available to investors at the time of the issue or offer?
controls.question_why: Investors must have the offer document at the point of decision; delayed availability defeats the purpose.
sufficiency_questions: Is the offer document available to investors at the time of issue/offer?

controls.requirement_text: Do not discriminate among clients, save on ethical and commercial considerations.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(H)(4) prohibits discrimination among clients except on ethical/commercial considerations.
controls.question_primary: Do you treat clients without discrimination, save on ethical and commercial grounds?
controls.question_why: Arbitrary discrimination among clients is a Code breach; ethical/commercial distinctions are permitted.
evidence_options: Documented basis for any differential treatment
sufficiency_questions: Is client treatment governed by a policy?
Is any differential treatment justified on ethical/commercial grounds?

controls.condition: you carry on activities other than investment banking
controls.requirement_text: Maintain an arm's-length relationship between the IB activity and any other activity carried on.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(H)(5) requires an arm's-length relationship between the IB activity and any other activity.
controls.question_primary: Do you carry on any activity other than investment banking?
controls.question_why: Blurring IB and other lines invites conflicts and cross-subsidy findings.
sufficiency_questions: Is IB activity kept at arm's length from your other activities?
Are conflicts across activities managed?

controls.requirement_text: On each issue, clearly demarcate the responsibilities of the various intermediaries.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(H)(6) requires responsibilities of the various intermediaries to be clearly demarcated.
controls.question_primary: On each issue, are the responsibilities of the various intermediaries clearly demarcated?
controls.question_why: Undefined roles among intermediaries create confusion and accountability gaps on an issue.
evidence_options: Engagement letters defining each intermediary's scope
sufficiency_questions: Are intermediary responsibilities documented per issue?

controls.condition: you deal in securities in Foreign Jurisdictions
controls.requirement_text: Where dealing in securities in Foreign Jurisdictions, comply with the Global Access norms and requirements specified by the Authority (until such norms are issued, Chapter V of the 2021 Regulations continues to apply per Reg 47).
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 27 requires a CMI dealing in securities in Foreign Jurisdictions to comply with the Authority's Global Access norms.
controls.question_primary: Do you deal in securities in Foreign Jurisdictions (Global Access)?
controls.question_why: Foreign-jurisdiction dealing sits under a distinct Global Access framework; operating outside it is a supervisory concern.
sufficiency_questions: Are your foreign-jurisdiction dealings within the Authority's Global Access norms (or Chapter V of the 2021 Regulations pending those norms)?

controls.clause_ref: Reg 26(1); Schedule II Part B(A), cl. 1
controls.requirement_text: Comply with the Act and the rules, regulations and bye-laws issued by the Government of India, the Authority and the recognised stock exchange.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 26(1) read with Schedule II Part B(A)(1) requires a broker dealer to comply with the applicable Act, rules, regulations and bye-laws of the recognised stock exchange.
controls.question_primary: Do you comply with the applicable bye-laws, rules and regulations of your recognised stock exchange?
controls.question_why: Exchange bye-law breaches are the fastest route to disciplinary action against a broker dealer.
sufficiency_questions: Do you track and comply with the exchange's bye-laws, rules and circulars?
Are exchange filings and obligations current?

controls.requirement_text: Do not engage in excessive speculative business beyond reasonable levels not commensurate with the broker dealer's financial soundness.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(A)(3) prohibits excessive speculative business beyond levels commensurate with financial soundness.
controls.question_primary: Do you keep proprietary/speculative exposure within levels commensurate with your financial soundness?
controls.question_why: Speculative exposure out of step with net worth is both a prudential and a conduct concern.
sufficiency_questions: Are exposure limits set against financial soundness?
Are they monitored and enforced?

controls.requirement_text: Faithfully execute client orders at the best available price; do not refuse a small investor merely on volume grounds; promptly inform clients of execution/non-execution and make prompt payment and delivery.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(A)(4)-(5) require best-execution, non-refusal of small investors, and prompt confirmation, payment and delivery.
controls.question_primary: Do you execute client orders at best available price and settle payments/deliveries promptly?
controls.question_why: Best-execution and prompt settlement are core investor-protection duties for a broker dealer.
sufficiency_questions: Are orders executed at best available price without volume-based refusal?
Are execution status, payments and deliveries handled promptly?

controls.requirement_text: Issue a contract note to the client without delay for all transactions, in the form specified by the recognised stock exchange.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(A)(6) requires contract notes to be issued without delay in the exchange-specified form.
controls.question_primary: Do you issue contract notes to clients without delay, in the exchange-specified form?
controls.question_why: A missing or delayed contract note is a documentary breach that surfaces immediately on inspection.
sufficiency_questions: Is a contract note issued for every transaction?
Is it in the exchange-specified form and issued without delay?

controls.requirement_text: Do not encourage sales/purchases with the sole object of generating brokerage; do not furnish false or misleading quotations, advice or information to induce business.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(A)(7)-(8) prohibit churning for brokerage and false/misleading quotes or advice.
controls.question_primary: Do you have controls against churning and against false or misleading quotes/advice to clients?
controls.question_why: Inducing trades through misleading information or churning is a conduct breach with enforcement exposure.
sufficiency_questions: Are staff barred from churning to generate brokerage?
Is client-facing information checked for accuracy?

controls.requirement_text: Do not knowingly deal for a client who has failed to meet commitments to another broker dealer; do not use unfair means to induce clients away from other broker dealers.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(A)(9)-(10) prohibit dealing for defaulting clients of other broker dealers and unfair inducement of clients.
controls.question_primary: Do you avoid dealing for known defaulting clients of other broker dealers and avoid unfair inducement of their clients?
controls.question_why: These inter-broker conduct rules protect market integrity and peer relationships.
sufficiency_questions: Do onboarding checks flag defaults with other broker dealers?
Is client solicitation conducted by fair means?

controls.clause_ref: Reg 26(2); Schedule II Part B(A), cl. 2
controls.requirement_text: Comply with the Act and the rules, regulations and bye-laws issued by the Government of India, the Authority and the recognised clearing corporation.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 26(2) read with Schedule II Part B(A)(2) requires a clearing member to comply with the applicable Act, rules, regulations and bye-laws of the recognised clearing corporation.
controls.question_primary: Do you comply with the applicable bye-laws, rules and regulations of your recognised clearing corporation?
controls.question_why: Clearing-corporation bye-law compliance underpins your clearing and settlement rights.
sufficiency_questions: Do you track and comply with the clearing corporation's bye-laws, rules and circulars?
Are margin and settlement obligations met on time?

controls.requirement_text: Enter into a written agreement with each client whose securities/products it rates, setting out the rights and liabilities of each party and the fee.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 28(1) requires a written rating agreement with each client covering rights, liabilities and fee.
controls.question_primary: Do you have a written rating agreement with each rated client covering rights, liabilities and fee?
controls.question_why: The rating agreement is the foundational document for each engagement; its absence is a clear gap.
sufficiency_questions: Is an agreement in place for every rated client?
Does it set out rights, liabilities and fee?

controls.requirement_text: Inform the client of the rating assigned, and continuously monitor and periodically review each rating unless it is withdrawn.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 28(3)-(4) require informing the client of the rating and continuous monitoring with periodic review.
controls.question_primary: Do you inform clients of assigned ratings and continuously monitor/periodically review them?
controls.question_why: Stale or unmonitored ratings mislead the market and are a core supervisory concern for a CRA.
sufficiency_questions: Are clients informed of the assigned rating?
Are ratings under continuous monitoring with periodic reviews?

controls.condition: you withdraw a rating while obligations under the rated instrument are outstanding
controls.requirement_text: Do not withdraw a rating while obligations under the rated instrument are outstanding except in the permitted situations, and state the reason for withdrawal in the press release.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 28(5) restricts rating withdrawals to permitted situations and requires the reason to be stated in the press release.
controls.question_primary: Have you withdrawn any rating during the FY under review?
controls.question_why: Improper withdrawal removes information the market relies on; the permitted grounds are narrow.
sufficiency_questions: Was each withdrawal within a permitted situation?
Was the reason stated in the press release?

controls.requirement_text: Disseminate information on rating changes promptly through press releases and simultaneously to the recognised stock exchange (where the product is listed in an IFSC).
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 28(6) requires prompt dissemination of rating changes via press releases and to the recognised stock exchange where listed.
controls.question_primary: Do you disseminate rating changes promptly via press release and to the exchange where listed?
controls.question_why: Delayed dissemination of a rating change is a market-integrity failure with immediate consequences.
sufficiency_questions: Are rating changes released promptly?
Are listed-product changes sent simultaneously to the exchange?

controls.requirement_text: Make public the rating definitions and symbols with a statement that ratings are not buy/hold/sell recommendations, and make public the rationale of ratings covering underlying factors.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 28(7)-(8) require public disclosure of rating definitions/symbols with the non-recommendation statement and the rating rationale.
controls.question_primary: Do you publish rating definitions/symbols (with the non-recommendation caveat) and the rationale of your ratings?
controls.question_why: Transparency of meaning and rationale is what makes a rating usable and defensible.
sufficiency_questions: Are definitions, symbols and the non-recommendation statement public?
Is a rationale published for ratings?

controls.requirement_text: Specify the rating process and file a copy of it with the Authority for record.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 28(9) requires the rating process to be specified and a copy filed with the Authority.
controls.question_primary: Have you documented your rating process and filed a copy with the Authority?
controls.question_why: A filed, documented process is the baseline the Authority checks your practice against.
sufficiency_questions: Is the rating process documented?
Has a copy been filed with the Authority?

controls.requirement_text: Constitute professional rating committees of adequately qualified and knowledgeable members, and take all rating decisions through such committees.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 28(10) requires qualified rating committees to take all rating decisions.
controls.question_primary: Are all rating decisions taken by a professional rating committee of qualified members?
controls.question_why: Committee-based decisions guard against single-analyst bias and are a governance expectation.
sufficiency_questions: Is a qualified rating committee constituted?
Are all rating decisions taken by the committee?

controls.requirement_text: Exercise due diligence to ensure the rating given is fair and appropriate.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 28(11) requires due diligence so that ratings are fair and appropriate.
controls.question_primary: Do you exercise documented due diligence so ratings are fair and appropriate?
controls.question_why: Due-diligence trails are what defend a rating if it is later questioned.
sufficiency_questions: Is there a documented due-diligence basis for ratings?
Are ratings supported by adequate research?

controls.requirement_text: Do not rate securities or products issued by the CRA itself or any of its group entities.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 28(12) prohibits rating securities/products of the CRA itself or its group entities.
controls.question_primary: Do you have controls preventing you from rating your own or any group entity's securities?
controls.question_why: Rating a related issuer is a fundamental conflict that voids the rating's credibility.
sufficiency_questions: Do you screen issuers against the CRA and its group entities?
Are self/group ratings excluded?

controls.clause_ref: Reg 28(13); Schedule II Part B(B), cl. 9
controls.requirement_text: Maintain procedures and systems to prevent trading on, and misuse of, unpublished price sensitive information (including prior knowledge of rating decisions/changes) obtained during assignments.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 28(13) and Schedule II Part B(B)(9) require controls preventing trading on and misuse of UPSI, including prior knowledge of rating actions.
controls.question_primary: Do you have controls preventing trading on or misuse of UPSI (including advance knowledge of rating actions)?
controls.question_why: Advance knowledge of a rating action is potent UPSI; leakage or trading on it is a grave breach.
sufficiency_questions: Does the policy cover prior knowledge of rating decisions/changes?
Are there operational controls (restricted list / access limits / pre-clearance)?

controls.requirement_text: Maintain an arm's-length relationship between the credit rating activity and the CRA's other activities.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(B)(2) requires an arm's-length relationship between rating activity and other activities.
controls.question_primary: Do you keep the rating activity at arm's length from your other activities?
controls.question_why: Blurring rating and other lines invites conflict and cross-influence findings.
sufficiency_questions: Is rating activity segregated from other activities?
Are cross-activity conflicts managed?

controls.clause_ref: Reg 29(1); Schedule II Part B(C), cl. 7
controls.requirement_text: Separate and segregate custodian activities from all other activities, maintaining an arm's-length relationship in staff and systems.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 29(1) and Schedule II Part B(C)(7) require custodian activities to be separated and segregated from all other activities at arm's length.
controls.question_primary: Do you separate and segregate your custodian activities (staff and systems) from all other activities?
controls.question_why: Segregation protects client assets from contamination by the custodian's other business risks.
sufficiency_questions: Are custodian activities segregated from other activities?
Is separation maintained in both staff and systems?

controls.requirement_text: Maintain adequate mechanisms for reviewing, monitoring and evaluating the custodian's controls, systems, procedures and safeguards.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 29(2) requires mechanisms to review, monitor and evaluate controls, systems, procedures and safeguards.
controls.question_primary: Do you review, monitor and evaluate your custody controls, systems and safeguards?
controls.question_why: Custody without an oversight loop drifts out of control between audits.
sufficiency_questions: Is there a mechanism to review and monitor controls?
Are reviews evidenced?

controls.requirement_text: Enter into an agreement with each client detailing the various circumstances relating to custody of securities/products or funds.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 29(3) requires a custody agreement with each client detailing custody circumstances.
controls.question_primary: Do you have a custody agreement with each client detailing custody arrangements?
controls.question_why: The custody agreement defines duties and liability; gaps here expose both sides.
sufficiency_questions: Is an agreement in place for every client?
Does it detail the custody circumstances?

controls.clause_ref: Reg 29(4); Schedule II Part B(C), cl. 4-5
controls.requirement_text: Maintain internal controls to prevent manipulation of records and documents and to protect records from theft and natural hazard, with continuity and back-up so records are not lost or destroyed and can be traced / title documents duplicated.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 29(4) and Schedule II Part B(C)(4)-(5) require controls against record manipulation/loss, with continuity, back-up and traceability.
controls.question_primary: Do you have controls protecting custody records from manipulation, theft, hazard and loss, with back-ups?
controls.question_why: Loss or tampering of custody records directly threatens client title to assets.
sufficiency_questions: Are records protected against manipulation, theft and hazard?
Is there continuity and back-up so records can be traced/reconstructed?

controls.requirement_text: Be prompt in distributing dividends, interest or other income accruals received or collected on behalf of clients on securities held in custody.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(C)(1) requires prompt distribution of income accruals to clients.
controls.question_primary: Do you promptly distribute dividends, interest and other accruals to clients?
controls.question_why: Delayed pass-through of client income is a direct client-detriment finding.
sufficiency_questions: Are client income accruals distributed promptly?
Is timing tracked?

controls.requirement_text: Remain continuously accountable for the movement of securities and cash in and out of the custody account, and provide a complete audit trail whenever called for by the client or the Authority.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(C)(2) requires continuous accountability and a complete audit trail of securities and cash movements.
controls.question_primary: Can you produce a complete audit trail of every securities and cash movement on demand?
controls.question_why: An incomplete audit trail on client assets is among the most serious custody findings.
sufficiency_questions: Is every securities/cash movement recorded?
Can a complete audit trail be produced on demand?

controls.requirement_text: Maintain adequate, well-documented infrastructure and operations manuals; extend cooperation to other custodians, depositories and clearing organisations for inter-custodial settlements; and exercise due diligence in safekeeping and administration of client assets.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(C)(3),(6),(8) require documented infrastructure, inter-custodial cooperation and due diligence in safekeeping.
controls.question_primary: Do you have documented custody operations and exercise due diligence in safekeeping client assets?
controls.question_why: Documented operations and cooperation are what keep settlements and safekeeping reliable.
sufficiency_questions: Are operations documented and backed by manuals?
Is due diligence exercised in safekeeping and settlements?

controls.requirement_text: Enter into an agreement with the issuer before the opening of the subscription list for the issue of debentures.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 30(1) requires a debenture-trustee agreement with the issuer before the subscription list opens.
controls.question_primary: Do you execute the trustee agreement with the issuer before the subscription list opens?
controls.question_why: A late trustee agreement undermines the protection debenture holders are entitled to from the outset.
sufficiency_questions: Is an agreement signed before the subscription list opens for each issue?

controls.requirement_text: Do not act as debenture trustee where you are an associate of the issuer or are likely to have a conflict of interest in any manner.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 30(2) bars acting as trustee where the trustee is an associate of the issuer or likely to have a conflict of interest.
controls.question_primary: Do you screen each mandate to ensure you are not an associate of, or conflicted with, the issuer?
controls.question_why: Acting for a connected issuer defeats the trustee's protective role for debenture holders.
sufficiency_questions: Do you screen for associate status and conflicts before accepting?
Do you decline where conflicted?

controls.requirement_text: Accept a trust deed containing standard and issue-specific information, consistent with the terms of the proposed issue, and free of covenants prejudicial to debenture holders.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 30(3)(a)-(b) require an appropriate trust deed consistent with issue terms and free of prejudicial covenants.
controls.question_primary: Are your trust deeds consistent with the issue terms and free of covenants prejudicial to holders?
controls.question_why: The trust deed is the debenture holders' core protection; defective deeds carry through the whole issue.
sufficiency_questions: Does the deed carry standard and issue-specific information?
Is it consistent with the issue and free of prejudicial covenants?

controls.requirement_text: Call for periodical / performance reports and fund-utilisation reports (within 7 days of the relevant board meeting or 45 days of the quarter, whichever is earlier) and obtain lead-bank reports on project progress.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 30(3)(c),(d),(k),(r) require periodic performance and fund-utilisation reports within the stated timelines and lead-bank progress reports.
controls.question_primary: Do you call for periodic performance and fund-utilisation reports within the prescribed timelines?
controls.question_why: Timely monitoring reports are how a trustee catches issuer distress early.
sufficiency_questions: Are reports called for within 7 days of the board meeting or 45 days of the quarter, whichever earlier?
Are fund-utilisation and lead-bank reports obtained?

controls.condition: a default or breach of the issue terms or trust-deed covenants arises
controls.requirement_text: On any default or breach of the issue terms / trust-deed covenants, take reasonable remedial steps, communicate defaults to debenture holders, and inform the Authority immediately of any breach of the trust deed or applicable law.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 30(3)(e),(g),(q) require communication of defaults to holders, remedial steps on breach, and immediate intimation to the Authority.
controls.question_primary: Did any default or breach of the issue terms / trust deed arise during the FY under review?
controls.question_why: Silence on a default is itself the breach; holders and the Authority must be told at once.
sufficiency_questions: Were defaults communicated to debenture holders?
Was the Authority informed immediately and were remedial steps taken?

controls.condition: two consecutive interest defaults, a security-creation default, or a redemption default occurs
controls.requirement_text: On two consecutive defaults in interest payment, or default in creation of security, or default in redemption, appoint a nominee director on the issuer's board.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 30(3)(f) requires appointment of a nominee director on the issuer's board on the specified defaults.
controls.question_primary: Did a trigger for nominee-director appointment (two consecutive interest defaults / security-creation default / redemption default) arise this FY?
controls.question_why: The nominee-director right is a key protective lever; failing to invoke it on trigger is a lapse.
sufficiency_questions: Was a nominee director appointed on the issuer's board on the trigger?

controls.requirement_text: Ensure security creation, debenture redemption reserve and recovery expense fund conditions are satisfied; that issuer/guarantor assets suffice and are unencumbered; perform acts necessary to enforce security and protect holders; and exercise independent due diligence before creating a charge (security free of encumbrance or consents obtained).
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 30(3)(h),(i),(j),(n) and 30(4) require verification of security/DRR/REF conditions, sufficiency and freedom of assets, enforcement of security and independent charge-creation due diligence.
controls.question_primary: Do you verify security creation, DRR/REF, asset sufficiency and charge status with independent due diligence?
controls.question_why: Weak security verification is exactly what leaves debenture holders exposed on default.
sufficiency_questions: Are security, DRR and recovery-expense-fund conditions verified?
Is independent due diligence done before charge creation (encumbrance-free or consents obtained)?

controls.condition: you seek to relinquish a debenture-trustee assignment
controls.requirement_text: Do not relinquish the debenture-trustee assignment for any issuer's debenture issue unless and until another debenture trustee is appointed in its place by the issuer.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 30(5) bars relinquishing the assignment until a replacement trustee is appointed.
controls.question_primary: Did you seek to relinquish any debenture-trustee assignment this FY?
controls.question_why: Leaving an issue without a trustee strands the debenture holders' protection.
sufficiency_questions: Was a replacement trustee appointed before you relinquished?

controls.requirement_text: Make adequate, timely and comprehensible disclosures to debenture holders; establish the true and full identity and financial situation of each client with records; share client-company information with credit rating agencies where required; and avoid misrepresentation.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(D)(1)-(4) require comprehensible timely disclosures, client identity/financial records, information-sharing with CRAs and avoidance of misrepresentation.
controls.question_primary: Do you make timely, comprehensible disclosures to debenture holders and keep proper client identity/financial records?
controls.question_why: Balanced, timely disclosure is what lets debenture holders act to protect themselves.
sufficiency_questions: Are disclosures to holders timely and comprehensible?
Are client identity and financial records maintained, with CRA sharing where required?

controls.requirement_text: Comply with the applicable laws, including bye-laws, rules and regulations, specified by the recognised depository.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 31(1) requires compliance with the recognised depository's bye-laws, rules and regulations.
controls.question_primary: Do you comply with the bye-laws, rules and regulations of your recognised depository?
controls.question_why: Depository bye-law compliance underpins your standing as a participant.
sufficiency_questions: Do you track and comply with the depository's bye-laws, rules and circulars?

controls.requirement_text: Open separate accounts in the name of each beneficial owner and segregate each beneficial owner's securities, without mixing them with other beneficial owners' securities or the participant's own.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 31(2) requires separate accounts per beneficial owner and full segregation of their securities.
controls.question_primary: Do you keep each beneficial owner's securities in separate, segregated accounts (never mixed with others' or your own)?
controls.question_why: Commingling beneficial owners' holdings is a direct threat to their title and a serious finding.
sufficiency_questions: Is a separate account maintained per beneficial owner?
Are their securities segregated from others' and from proprietary holdings?

controls.requirement_text: Maintain adequate mechanisms for reviewing, monitoring and evaluating internal accounting controls and systems.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 31(3) requires mechanisms to review, monitor and evaluate internal accounting controls and systems.
controls.question_primary: Do you review, monitor and evaluate your internal accounting controls and systems?
controls.question_why: Unchecked accounting systems accumulate errors that surface as reconciliation breaks.
sufficiency_questions: Is there a mechanism to review internal accounting controls?
Are reviews evidenced?

controls.clause_ref: Reg 31(4); Schedule II Part B(E), cl. 3
controls.requirement_text: Where records are maintained electronically, ensure the integrity of the data processing system at all times, with continuity and up-to-date back-up so data/records are not lost or destroyed.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 31(4) and Schedule II Part B(E)(3) require data-processing integrity and up-to-date back-up for electronic records.
controls.question_primary: Do you maintain data-processing integrity and up-to-date back-ups for your electronic records?
controls.question_why: A DP's records are the register of client holdings; integrity and back-up are non-negotiable.
sufficiency_questions: Is data-processing integrity maintained at all times?
Is up-to-date back-up available?

controls.requirement_text: Reconcile the participant's records with the depository on a daily basis.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 31(5) requires daily reconciliation of the participant's records with the depository.
controls.question_primary: Do you reconcile your records with the depository every day?
controls.question_why: A missed daily reconciliation lets discrepancies in client holdings go undetected.
sufficiency_questions: Is reconciliation performed daily?
Are breaks investigated and resolved?

controls.requirement_text: Do not increase charges/fees without at least 7 days' advance notice to beneficial owners; be prompt and diligent in account opening, dispatch of DRF/RRF, execution of debit instruction slips and other activities undertaken for beneficial owners.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(E)(1)-(2) require 7-day advance fee notice and prompt, diligent processing of beneficial-owner instructions.
controls.question_primary: Do you give 7 days' notice before fee increases and process beneficial-owner instructions promptly?
controls.question_why: Notice and prompt processing are the day-to-day conduct tests a DP is judged on.
sufficiency_questions: Is at least 7 days' notice given before any fee increase?
Are account opening, DRF/RRF and DIS handled promptly?

controls.requirement_text: Distribute only capital-market products/services that have been authorised, vetted or approved for the relevant investor class by the home regulator, and comply with all applicable laws in the jurisdictions of issuers, service providers and clients.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 32(2)-(3) require distributing only products authorised for the investor class and complying with all applicable jurisdictional laws.
controls.question_primary: Do you distribute only products authorised for the relevant investor class, complying with all applicable jurisdictional laws?
controls.question_why: Distributing an unauthorised or wrongly-targeted product is a direct regulatory and mis-selling exposure.
sufficiency_questions: Are products confirmed as authorised for the target investor class?
Do you comply with issuer/service-provider/client jurisdiction laws?

controls.requirement_text: Avoid mis-selling; consider clients' interest and suitability to their financial needs; act in clients' best interests and inform a client where a product/service is not suitable for them.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(F)(1)-(3) require avoidance of mis-selling, suitability assessment and acting in the client's best interest.
controls.question_primary: Do you assess suitability, avoid mis-selling and tell clients when a product is unsuitable?
controls.question_why: Mis-selling is the single most common and most damaging distributor finding.
sufficiency_questions: Is suitability assessed before distribution?
Are clients told when a product is unsuitable?

controls.requirement_text: For clients other than sophisticated investors, undertake product due diligence and suitability assessment (seeking financial status, experience and objectives); for sophisticated investors, obtain a declaration that they understand the associated risks.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(F)(2),(5) require due diligence/suitability for non-sophisticated clients and a risk-understanding declaration from sophisticated investors.
controls.question_primary: Do you run due diligence/suitability for non-sophisticated clients and obtain risk declarations from sophisticated investors?
controls.question_why: The evidentiary trail differs by investor class; missing either is a conduct gap.
sufficiency_questions: Is due diligence/suitability done for non-sophisticated clients?
Are risk declarations held from sophisticated investors?

controls.requirement_text: Disclose all material information (business, disciplinary history, terms, conflicts, affiliations); disclose remuneration and its basis on client request; provide full and latest product information, clearly highlighting assumptions and risks.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(F)(6),(8),(11) require material, remuneration and full product-information disclosures.
controls.question_primary: Do you make full material, remuneration and product disclosures (with assumptions and risks highlighted)?
controls.question_why: Thin disclosure is what turns a sale into a mis-sale in hindsight.
sufficiency_questions: Are material and product disclosures complete and current?
Is remuneration disclosed on request?

controls.requirement_text: Give no assurance or misrepresentation of returns/risk; do not attract clients through rebates, kickbacks or gifts; do not encourage over-transacting or churning; keep clients' interest paramount over remuneration; and avoid manipulative, fraudulent or deceptive practices.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(F)(12),(13),(22),(23),(24) prohibit misrepresentation, inducements, churning and deceptive practices, with client interest paramount.
controls.question_primary: Do you have controls against return assurances, inducements, churning and deceptive practices?
controls.question_why: These are the practices enforcement looks for first in a distribution book.
sufficiency_questions: Are return assurances, rebates/gifts and churning prohibited and monitored?
Is client interest placed above remuneration?

controls.requirement_text: Take all reasonable steps to avoid conflicts of interest with policies to identify, manage, monitor and disclose them; and where multiple activities are undertaken, segregate the activities with proper disclosure to clients.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(F)(18)-(19) require a conflict-of-interest framework and segregation of multiple activities with disclosure.
controls.question_primary: Do you have a conflict-of-interest framework and segregate multiple activities with disclosure?
controls.question_why: Undisclosed conflicts across activities quietly bias what gets sold.
sufficiency_questions: Is there a COI policy identifying and managing conflicts?
Are multiple activities segregated and disclosed?

controls.requirement_text: Ensure clear segregation of proprietary investments from those carried out as part of distribution activities, and where an omnibus structure is used, comply with all applicable norms.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(F)(15) requires segregation of proprietary and distribution investments and omnibus compliance.
controls.question_primary: Do you segregate proprietary investments from distribution activity (and comply with omnibus norms if used)?
controls.question_why: Mixing proprietary and client flows invites front-running and allocation abuse.
sufficiency_questions: Is proprietary activity segregated from distribution?
Are omnibus norms complied with where used?

controls.requirement_text: Maintain adequate client records (including suitability correspondence and client consent/dissent), in physical or digital form, and ensure all statutory and agreed communications are reliably and timely sent to clients.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(F)(16)-(17) require adequate client records and timely statutory/agreed communications.
controls.question_primary: Do you maintain complete client records and send statutory/agreed communications on time?
controls.question_why: Records of suitability and consent are what defend a distribution decision after the fact.
sufficiency_questions: Are client records complete (suitability, consent/dissent)?
Are statutory/agreed communications sent reliably and on time?

controls.requirement_text: Assist clients with KYC and related procedures and compliance with AML/CFT laws to the extent applicable, and do not tamper with (insert, delete or change) client application forms or documents.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(F)(9)-(10) require KYC/AML assistance and prohibit tampering with client documents.
controls.question_primary: Do you assist clients with KYC/AML and have controls against tampering with client documents?
controls.question_why: Document tampering and weak KYC assistance are both serious integrity failures.
sufficiency_questions: Do you assist with KYC/AML as applicable?
Are there controls preventing alteration of client documents?

controls.clause_ref: Schedule II Part B(F), cl. 26-31 (Advertisement Code)
controls.condition: you issue advertisements for capital-market products or services
controls.requirement_text: Where advertising, ensure advertisements are accurate, true, fair, clear, complete, unambiguous and concise; not false/misleading/biased/deceptive; carry no testimonials or rankings; and stay consistent with the PPM / disclosure document.
controls.regulatory_basis: Schedule II Part B(F)(26)-(31) set the Advertisement Code for distributors.
controls.question_primary: Do you issue advertisements for capital-market products or services?
controls.question_why: A single misleading advertisement can taint the whole distribution book.
evidence_options: Consistency check vs PPM / disclosure document
sufficiency_questions: Are advertisements accurate, fair and free of testimonials/rankings?
Are they consistent with the PPM / disclosure document?

category_applicability: ESG Ratings and Data Products Provider
controls.requirement_text: Provide only services relating to ESG Ratings and ESG Data Products (including permitted external review for ESG-labelled bonds); undertake no other service without the prior approval of the Authority.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 33(1)-(2) limit an ERDPP to ESG Ratings/Data Products services and bar other services without prior Authority approval.
controls.question_primary: Do you confine yourself to ESG Ratings/Data Products services (and seek prior approval for anything else)?
controls.question_why: Stepping outside the permitted activity without approval is a registration-scope breach.
sufficiency_questions: Are services limited to ESG Ratings/Data Products (and permitted external review)?
Is prior approval held for any other service?

category_applicability: ESG Ratings and Data Products Provider
controls.requirement_text: On a comply-or-explain basis, maintain good-governance arrangements and written policies and procedures designed to ensure the issuance of high-quality ESG Ratings and Data Products.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 33(3)(a)-(b) require good-governance arrangements and quality policies/procedures on a comply-or-explain basis.
controls.question_primary: Do you have governance arrangements and written quality policies for your ESG products?
controls.question_why: The comply-or-explain code still expects the policy to exist or a documented explanation for its absence.
sufficiency_questions: Are governance arrangements in place?
Are written quality policies maintained (or the deviation explained)?

category_applicability: ESG Ratings and Data Products Provider
controls.requirement_text: Adopt written policies and procedures ensuring decisions are independent and free from interference, and identify, avoid, manage, mitigate and disclose actual or potential conflicts of interest.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 33(3)(c) requires conflict-of-interest policies safeguarding independence, on a comply-or-explain basis.
controls.question_primary: Do you have conflict-of-interest controls safeguarding the independence of your ESG assessments?
controls.question_why: Compromised independence is fatal to the credibility of an ESG rating.
sufficiency_questions: Do policies safeguard independence from interference?
Are conflicts identified, managed and disclosed?

category_applicability: ESG Ratings and Data Products Provider
controls.requirement_text: Prioritise public disclosure and transparency of ESG Ratings/Data Products, including methodologies and processes; disclose the rating methodology and all ESG Ratings provided, on the website.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 33(3)(d),(5),(6) require public transparency of methodologies and disclosure of methodology and all ESG Ratings on the website.
controls.question_primary: Do you publish your ESG methodologies and all ESG Ratings on your website?
controls.question_why: Opaque ESG methodology defeats the product's purpose and the code's transparency principle.
sufficiency_questions: Are methodologies and processes publicly disclosed?
Are all ESG Ratings disclosed on the website?

category_applicability: ESG Ratings and Data Products Provider
controls.requirement_text: Adopt written policies and procedures to protect all non-public information received or communicated in relation to ESG Ratings and Data Products.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 33(3)(e) requires confidentiality policies for non-public information, on a comply-or-explain basis.
controls.question_primary: Do you have confidentiality controls for non-public information used in your ESG products?
controls.question_why: Leakage of entity-supplied non-public data breaches both confidence and the code.
sufficiency_questions: Is non-public information protected by policy and controls?

category_applicability: ESG Ratings and Data Products Provider
controls.requirement_text: Maintain efficient engagement/information-gathering processes with rated entities and address flagged issues while preserving independence; disclose comply-or-explain compliance with the Code on the website; and segregate ESG Ratings from ESG Data Products activities to avoid conflict of interest.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 33(3)(f),(4),(7) require sound engagement processes, website comply-or-explain disclosure and segregation of ESG Ratings and Data Products activities.
controls.question_primary: Do you run sound engagement processes, publish comply-or-explain compliance, and segregate ratings from data-products activities?
controls.question_why: Engagement quality and activity segregation are what keep ESG outputs credible and conflict-free.
sufficiency_questions: Are engagement processes maintained and issues addressed independently?
Is comply-or-explain disclosed and are ratings/data-products activities segregated?

controls.requirement_text: Disclose to prospective clients all material information about itself (business, disciplinary history, terms, affiliations) and, for recommended products, disclose holdings/positions, conflicts, key features and performance track record, and applicable warnings/disclaimers.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 34(1)-(2) require material self-disclosures and product-level disclosures (positions, conflicts, features, warnings) to clients.
controls.question_primary: Do you make full material self- and product-disclosures to clients before advising?
controls.question_why: Undisclosed positions or conflicts undermine the very advice being given.
sufficiency_questions: Are self-disclosures (business, disciplinary, terms, affiliations) made?
Are positions, conflicts, features and warnings disclosed for recommendations?

controls.requirement_text: Act in a fiduciary capacity towards clients and disclose all conflicts of interest as and when they arise.
controls.regulatory_basis: Regulation 34(3) requires the adviser to act in a fiduciary capacity and disclose conflicts as they arise.
controls.question_primary: Do you act in a fiduciary capacity and disclose conflicts as they arise?
controls.question_why: The fiduciary standard is the defining duty of an investment adviser.
sufficiency_questions: Is the fiduciary duty embedded in your process?
Are conflicts disclosed as they arise?
